messages.author: 3a71f645a046e485
messages.subject: Conditional mutate
parts:
Hi all, I need to do a couple of mutate() operations based on conditions. There are three cases, each of which is treated differently. I could use ifelse() for each one but that's cumbersome (and is it inefficient?). What I'm doing is making 3 dataframes using filter() and then mutate() and then rbind() to put the three together, like this:

summative.ratings.75 <- summative.ratings.0 %>%
    group_by(Teacher) %>%
        filter(obs_weight==.75) %>%
        mutate(adj.final.score=sum(adj.tp*obs_weight, summ_va, summ_pt, na.rm=T),
               plain.final.score=sum(plain.tp*obs_weight, summ_va, summ_pt, na.rm=T))

summative.ratings.90 <- summative.ratings.0 %>%
    group_by(Teacher) %>%
        filter(obs_weight==.90) %>%
        mutate(adj.final.score=sum(adj.tp*obs_weight, summ_pt, na.rm=T),
               plain.final.score=sum(plain.tp*obs_weight,summ_pt, na.rm=T))

summative.ratings.100 <- summative.ratings.0 %>%
    group_by(Teacher) %>%
        filter(obs_weight==1.0) %>%
        mutate(adj.final.score=sum(adj.tp*obs_weight, na.rm=T),
               plain.final.score=sum(plain.tp*obs_weight, na.rm=T))

summative.ratings <- rbind(summative.ratings.75, summative.ratings.90, summative.ratings.100)

I guess this works OK, but it's aesthetically displeasing. It seems there should be a more efficient, elegant way to do this, but I can't think of one. Can anyone else?

--
